note.explanation: A multicellular organism is organised in levels, from cells to organ systems. Different tissues and organs work together, and organ systems cooperate to keep the organism alive and its internal conditions stable.
examples: In a stomach, epithelial tissue produces secretions, while smooth muscle mixes food.
In a leaf, mesophyll carries out photosynthesis, while xylem transports water.
note.checkAnswer: Cells form tissues; tissues form organs; organs form organ systems.
note.simple: Small parts join together in an organised way. Cells make tissues, tissues make organs, and organs work together in organ systems.
note.checkQuestion: What is the correct order from cells to organ systems?
note.title: How living things are organised
steps: Cells with similar functions group together to form tissues.
Different tissues combine to form an organ.
Organs that work together form an organ system.
Organ systems work together to maintain the organism.

options: The sum of its parts is greater than the whole.
The individual parts are more important than the whole.
Its parts interact to perform more functions.
mcqs.stem: Q5.1. A higher level of organization exhibits emergent properties when:
rationales: This is incorrect because independent parts do not explain the new properties of the whole.
This is incorrect because emergent properties arise from interactions, not from the sum being greater than the whole.
This is incorrect because emergent properties depend on the coordinated whole, not the greater importance of separate parts.
This is correct because interactions between parts allow the higher level to perform more functions.

options: Cell → Organ → Tissue → Organelle → Organ system
Organelle → Cell → Tissue → Organ → Organ system
Tissue → Cell → Organelle → Organ → Organ system
Organ system → Tissue → Cell → Organelle → Organ
mcqs.stem: Q5.2. Which of the following demonstrates the levels of organization of the body, from simplest to most complex?
rationales: This is incorrect because tissues come before organs, and organelles come before cells.
This is correct because organelles form cells, cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs form organ systems.
This is incorrect because cells and organelles are placed in the wrong order.
This is incorrect because the sequence runs from more complex to simpler levels and then back to an organ.

options: Organ system level in the respiratory system
mcqs.stem: Q5.3. At which level of organization gas exchange occurs between body and environment?
rationales: This is incorrect because mitochondria use oxygen within cells rather than exchange gases with the environment.
This is incorrect because alveolar cells are involved in gas exchange, but the body-environment process is considered at the respiratory-system level.
This is incorrect because epithelial tissue contributes to exchange, but the complete process occurs through the respiratory system.
This is correct because the respiratory system exchanges gases between the body and the environment.

mcqs.stem: Q5.4. The epithelial tissue in the stomach wall is responsible for producing:
rationales: This is incorrect because stomach epithelium produces mucus as well as other secretions.
This is incorrect because it produces pepsinogen as well as other secretions.
This is incorrect because it produces hydrochloric acid as well as other secretions.
This is correct because stomach epithelial tissue produces mucus, pepsinogen, and hydrochloric acid.

mcqs.stem: Q5.5. In the wall of stomach, which tissue also contains blood vessels and nerves?
rationales: This is incorrect because the epithelial lining is not the tissue layer identified as containing the blood vessels and nerves.
This is incorrect because the muscle layer mainly contracts to move and mix food.
This is correct because the inner connective tissue contains blood vessels and nerves.
This is incorrect because the question identifies the inner connective tissue as the layer containing blood vessels and nerves.

mcqs.stem: Q5.6. In a leaf, which tissue is responsible for photosynthesis?
rationales: This is incorrect because xylem transports water and minerals.
This is correct because mesophyll tissue contains cells that carry out photosynthesis.
This is incorrect because the epidermis protects the leaf and helps regulate exchange.
This is incorrect because phloem transports food through the plant.

options: To transport sugars to other parts
To transport water to parts of leaf
To control the opening and closing of stomata
mcqs.stem: Q5.7. What is the primary function of the xylem tissue in a leaf?
rationales: This is incorrect because phloem transports sugars.
This is correct because xylem carries water to parts of the leaf.
This is incorrect because chlorophyll is present in photosynthetic cells, not synthesized by xylem as its primary function.
This is incorrect because guard cells control the opening and closing of stomata.

options: Storing minerals and producing blood cells
Filtering blood to remove waste products
mcqs.stem: Q5.8. Which of these is a function of the human skeletal system?
rationales: This is correct because bones store minerals and bone marrow produces blood cells.
This is incorrect because removal of carbon dioxide is a role of the respiratory system.
This is incorrect because filtering blood is chiefly a role of the kidneys in the excretory system.
This is incorrect because digestion breaks down food; the skeletal system does not do this.

mcqs.stem: Q5.9. Which structures are responsible for the transport of food in plant body?
rationales: This is incorrect because xylem transports water and minerals.
This is incorrect because palisade mesophyll carries out photosynthesis rather than transporting food around the plant.
This is correct because phloem transports food through the plant body.
This is incorrect because spongy mesophyll supports gas exchange within the leaf.

mcqs.stem: Q5.10. In a plant, which of the following is the primary function of the flower?
rationales: This is incorrect because transport of water and minerals is mainly carried out by xylem.
This is incorrect because supporting leaf growth is not the flower's primary function.
This is correct because the flower is involved in reproduction, including pollination.
This is incorrect because gas exchange is mainly regulated by stomata in leaves.

written.text: Q5.1. Enlist the levels of organization from cells to organ systems.
written.finalAnswer: Cell → Tissue → Organ → Organ system

rubric.why: The sequence must correctly identify the intermediate levels.
rubric.description: Give the tissue and organ levels in the correct order.
rubric.how: Write tissue after cell and organ after tissue.

rubric.why: The answer must finish with the requested highest level.
rubric.description: Give organ system as the final level.
rubric.how: Complete the sequence with organ system.

modelAnswer: Cell → Tissue → Organ → Organ system

written.text: Q5.2. What are the major roles of the epithelial tissue present in the stomach?
written.finalAnswer: It produces mucus, pepsinogen, and hydrochloric acid.

rubric.why: Mucus is a major stomach epithelial secretion.
rubric.how: State that epithelial tissue produces mucus.

rubric.why: The other major secretions complete the expected answer.
rubric.how: Include both secretions.

modelAnswer: The epithelial tissue of the stomach produces mucus, pepsinogen, and hydrochloric acid.

written.text: Q5.3. How do the smooth muscles contribute to the stomach’s function?
written.finalAnswer: They contract to churn and mix food with digestive juices and move it through the stomach.

rubric.why: Contraction and mixing are the key mechanical action of stomach smooth muscle.
rubric.description: Explain the muscle contractions that churn or mix food.
rubric.how: State that smooth muscles contract and churn or mix the food.

rubric.why: Mixing food with digestive juices supports digestion.
rubric.description: Connect muscle action to digestion or movement of food.
rubric.how: Mention mixing with digestive juices or moving food through the stomach.

modelAnswer: Smooth muscles contract to churn and mix food with digestive juices.
Their contractions also help move food through the stomach.

written.text: Q5.4. What is the function of the palisade mesophyll in the leaf?
written.finalAnswer: Palisade mesophyll carries out photosynthesis.

rubric.why: The answer must identify the leaf tissue asked about.
rubric.how: Refer directly to palisade mesophyll.

rubric.why: Photosynthesis is its principal function.
rubric.how: Say that it carries out photosynthesis.

modelAnswer: Palisade mesophyll contains many chloroplasts and carries out photosynthesis.

written.text: Q5.5. What is the role of the shoot system in plants?
written.finalAnswer: The shoot system supports the plant above ground and includes stems, leaves, flowers, and fruits; it helps with photosynthesis, transport, and reproduction.

rubric.why: Identifying shoot parts demonstrates what the system includes.
rubric.description: Name parts of the shoot system.
rubric.how: Include stems and leaves, or other shoot parts.

rubric.why: A function is needed to explain the system's role.
rubric.description: State a role of the shoot system.
rubric.how: Mention photosynthesis, transport, support, or reproduction.

modelAnswer: The shoot system includes the stem, leaves, flowers, and fruits.
It supports the plant and performs functions such as photosynthesis, transport, and reproduction.

written.text: Q5.6. What is homeostasis, and why is it important for organisms?
written.finalAnswer: Homeostasis is the maintenance of stable internal conditions; it is important because cells and organs need suitable conditions to function properly.

rubric.why: The definition must convey stability inside the organism.
rubric.how: State that it maintains stable internal conditions.

rubric.why: The importance is that life processes depend on suitable internal conditions.
rubric.how: Link stable conditions to proper cell or organ function.

modelAnswer: Homeostasis is the maintenance of stable internal conditions in an organism.
It is important because cells and organs need suitable conditions to function properly.

written.text: Q5.7. How does the human body maintain a stable internal temperature?
written.finalAnswer: The body uses temperature-regulating responses, including sweating to cool down and shivering to produce heat.

rubric.why: Sweating is a cooling response when body temperature rises.
rubric.description: Give a response that lowers body temperature.
rubric.how: State that the body sweats to lose heat.

rubric.why: Shivering helps generate heat when body temperature falls.
rubric.description: Give a response that raises body temperature.
rubric.how: State that shivering produces heat.

modelAnswer: If body temperature rises, sweating helps cool the body.
If body temperature falls, shivering produces heat and helps warm the body.

written.text: Q5.8. Differentiate between the following: i. Tissue and organ
written.finalAnswer: A tissue is a group of similar cells performing a particular function; an organ is made of different tissues working together to perform a function.

rubric.why: The tissue definition requires cells grouped by similarity and function.
rubric.how: Describe a tissue as similar cells working for a function.

rubric.why: An organ is distinguished by combining different tissues.
rubric.description: Define organ in contrast with tissue.
rubric.how: Explain that different tissues work together in an organ.

modelAnswer: A tissue is a group of similar cells that perform a particular function.
An organ is made of different tissues working together to perform a function.

written.text: Q5.8. Differentiate between the following: ii. Root system and shoot system
written.finalAnswer: The root system anchors the plant and absorbs water and minerals; the shoot system consists of above-ground stems, leaves, flowers, and fruits and performs support, photosynthesis, transport, and reproduction.

rubric.why: The root system is identified by its anchoring and absorption roles.
rubric.description: State a root-system feature or function.
rubric.how: Mention anchorage or absorption of water and minerals.

rubric.why: The shoot system must be distinguished by its parts or functions.
rubric.description: State a shoot-system feature or function.
rubric.how: Mention above-ground parts, photosynthesis, support, transport, or reproduction.

modelAnswer: The root system anchors the plant and absorbs water and minerals from the soil.
The shoot system includes stems, leaves, flowers, and fruits and carries out functions such as support, photosynthesis, transport, and reproduction.

written.text: Q5.8. Differentiate between the following: iii. Epidermal and mesophyll tissue
written.finalAnswer: Epidermal tissue forms the protective outer covering of the leaf; mesophyll lies inside the leaf and performs photosynthesis and gas exchange.

rubric.why: Protection is the key role of the epidermal tissue.
rubric.how: State that it forms the outer covering and protects the leaf.

rubric.why: Mesophyll is distinguished by its internal position and photosynthetic role.
rubric.how: State that it lies inside the leaf and carries out photosynthesis.

modelAnswer: Epidermal tissue forms the protective outer covering of the leaf.
Mesophyll tissue lies inside the leaf and performs photosynthesis; it also supports gas exchange.

written.text: Q5.8. Differentiate between the following: iv. Palisade and spongy mesophyll
written.finalAnswer: Palisade mesophyll has closely packed cells with many chloroplasts and carries out most photosynthesis; spongy mesophyll has loosely arranged cells with air spaces that help gas exchange.

rubric.why: The palisade layer is identified by its chloroplast-rich cells and photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Mention its many chloroplasts or its major role in photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Air spaces and gas exchange distinguish spongy mesophyll.
rubric.how: Mention its air spaces or gas-exchange role.

modelAnswer: Palisade mesophyll consists of closely packed cells with many chloroplasts and carries out most photosynthesis.
Spongy mesophyll has loosely arranged cells with air spaces that help gas exchange.

written.text: Q5.1. Explain the levels of organization in multicellular organism. How does each level contribute to the overall functioning of an organism?
written.finalAnswer: Organelles form cells, cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form organ systems, and organ systems work together to maintain the organism.

rubric.why: The answer must begin with the smallest listed levels in the correct order.
rubric.how: Show that organelles are parts of cells and similar cells form tissues.

rubric.why: Organs are formed from tissues working together.
rubric.how: State that different tissues form an organ.

rubric.why: The next organisation level is an organ system.
rubric.how: State that related organs form an organ system.

rubric.why: The levels contribute through coordinated function.
rubric.how: Describe cooperation between parts or systems.

rubric.why: The response must link the hierarchy to the functioning whole.
rubric.how: Explain that coordination supports the organism's life functions.

modelAnswer: An organelle is a specialised structure within a cell, and organelles help the cell perform its functions.
Cells with similar functions group together to form tissues.
Different tissues work together to form an organ, which performs particular functions.
Organs that work together form an organ system.
Organ systems coordinate their activities so the whole organism can function and maintain life.

written.text: Q5.2. What is a tissue level? Explain plant and animal tissues.
written.finalAnswer: The tissue level is a level of organization in which groups of similar cells work together to perform a particular function. Plant tissues include epidermal, mesophyll, xylem, and phloem tissues; animal tissues include epithelial, connective, muscle, and nervous tissues.

rubric.why: A definition of tissue level is essential.
rubric.how: Explain that similar cells work together for a function.

rubric.why: The answer must identify examples or types of plant tissues.
rubric.how: Name plant tissue types and, where useful, their roles.

rubric.why: The answer must identify examples or types of animal tissues.
rubric.how: Name animal tissue types.

rubric.why: The response should distinguish the two groups as parts of organism organisation.
rubric.description: Complete the comparison with both plant and animal tissues.
rubric.how: Include correct tissue examples for both groups.

modelAnswer: The tissue level is a level of organization in which groups of similar cells work together to perform a particular function.
Plant tissues include epidermal tissue, mesophyll, xylem, and phloem.
Epidermal tissue protects the plant, mesophyll carries out photosynthesis, xylem transports water, and phloem transports food.
Animal tissues include epithelial, connective, muscle, and nervous tissues, each specialised for particular functions.

written.text: Q5.3. Describe the tissue composition of the stomach. How does each tissue contribute to the digestive function of the stomach?
written.finalAnswer: The stomach has epithelial, connective, and muscle tissues. Epithelial tissue secretes mucus, pepsinogen, and hydrochloric acid; connective tissue supports the stomach and contains blood vessels and nerves; smooth muscle churns and mixes food with digestive juices.

rubric.why: Secretions from stomach epithelium contribute directly to digestion and protection.
rubric.description: Explain epithelial tissue and its secretions.
rubric.how: Name mucus, pepsinogen, and hydrochloric acid.

rubric.why: Connective tissue supports the stomach and contains important vessels and nerves.
rubric.how: Mention support and blood vessels or nerves.

rubric.why: Muscle movement mechanically mixes the stomach contents.
rubric.description: Explain the role of muscle tissue.
rubric.how: State that smooth muscle churns or mixes food.

rubric.why: The account must link the tissues to the stomach's digestive function.
rubric.how: Explain that food is mixed with digestive juices or chemically digested.

modelAnswer: The wall of the stomach contains epithelial, connective, and smooth muscle tissues.
The epithelial tissue produces mucus, pepsinogen, and hydrochloric acid, which protect the lining and aid digestion.
The connective tissue supports the stomach and contains blood vessels and nerves.
The smooth muscle contracts to churn food and mix it with digestive juices.

written.text: Q5.4. Describe the tissue composition of the leaf. How does each tissue contribute to the functions of the leaf?
written.finalAnswer: The leaf has epidermal tissue, mesophyll, and vascular tissues. The epidermis protects the leaf and its stomata regulate gas exchange; palisade mesophyll carries out most photosynthesis; spongy mesophyll allows gas exchange; xylem transports water and phloem transports food.

rubric.why: The outer protective tissue is a major component of the leaf.
rubric.how: Explain its protective role and optionally stomatal regulation.

rubric.why: Palisade mesophyll is the principal photosynthetic tissue.
rubric.how: State that it carries out most photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Spongy mesophyll contributes to gas exchange through its air spaces.
rubric.how: Mention air spaces and gas exchange.

rubric.why: Vascular tissues transport the substances needed by the leaf and plant.
rubric.how: State the transport roles of xylem and phloem.

modelAnswer: The leaf has epidermal tissue, mesophyll tissue, and vascular tissues.
The epidermis protects the leaf, while stomata in the epidermis allow regulated gas exchange.
Palisade mesophyll contains many chloroplasts and carries out most photosynthesis.
Spongy mesophyll has air spaces that support gas exchange.
Xylem brings water to the leaf, and phloem transports food from it to other parts of the plant.

written.text: Q5.5. How do the organ systems come together to form the human body?
written.finalAnswer: Different organ systems consist of organs that work together, and the systems coordinate with one another to perform life functions and maintain homeostasis in the human body.

rubric.why: The relationship between organs and systems establishes the organisation hierarchy.
rubric.description: Explain how organ systems are formed.
rubric.how: State that organs working together form organ systems.

rubric.why: The answer must describe the body as containing several systems.
rubric.description: Identify the systems as parts of the whole body.
rubric.how: Explain that many organ systems make up the body.

rubric.why: Coordination is central to the systems' combined function.
rubric.how: State that the systems coordinate or work together.

rubric.why: The final purpose is the functioning and maintenance of the body.
rubric.description: Give the result of system cooperation.
rubric.how: Link cooperation to life functions or homeostasis.

modelAnswer: Each organ system consists of organs that work together to carry out particular functions.
The human body contains several organ systems, such as the digestive, respiratory, circulatory, and excretory systems.
These systems work together and exchange materials needed by the body.
Their coordinated activities enable life functions and help maintain homeostasis.

written.text: Q5.6. Describe the roles of the digestive system and the excretory system in homeostasis.
written.finalAnswer: The digestive system breaks food down and absorbs nutrients and water; the excretory system removes metabolic wastes and helps regulate water and salt balance. Together they help keep the internal conditions stable.

rubric.why: Digestion makes food materials available to the organism.
rubric.how: Describe breakdown of food and nutrient absorption.

rubric.why: Absorption supplies materials needed by cells.
rubric.how: Mention absorption of nutrients and/or water.

rubric.why: Waste removal is a central excretory role.
rubric.how: State that it removes metabolic wastes.

rubric.why: Both systems contribute to stable internal conditions.
rubric.how: Explain regulation of water balance or stable internal conditions.

modelAnswer: The digestive system breaks food into simpler substances and absorbs nutrients and water into the body.
The excretory system removes metabolic wastes from the body.
It also helps regulate the balance of water and salts.
Together, these systems help maintain stable internal conditions, or homeostasis.

written.text: Q5.7. Explain the functions of various plant organs.
written.finalAnswer: Roots anchor the plant and absorb water and minerals; stems support the plant and transport materials; leaves carry out photosynthesis and gas exchange; flowers support reproduction; fruits protect and help disperse seeds.

rubric.why: Root functions are essential to the plant's support and uptake.
rubric.how: Mention anchorage or absorption of water and minerals.

rubric.why: The stem supports the shoot and transports materials.
rubric.how: Mention support and/or transport.

rubric.why: Leaves are the main photosynthetic organs.
rubric.how: State that leaves carry out photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Flowers are reproductive organs.
rubric.how: Link flowers with reproduction or pollination.

rubric.why: Fruits protect or help disperse seeds.
rubric.how: Mention seed protection or dispersal.

modelAnswer: Roots anchor the plant in the soil and absorb water and minerals.
Stems support the above-ground parts and transport water, minerals, and food.
Leaves carry out photosynthesis and allow gas exchange.
Flowers are involved in plant reproduction, including pollination.
Fruits protect seeds and may help disperse them.

written.text: Q5.8. Describe the structure and function of the plant root system.
written.finalAnswer: The root system consists of roots, usually growing below the ground. It anchors the plant, absorbs water and minerals from the soil, and may store food.

rubric.why: The structure must identify the root system as roots of the plant.
rubric.how: State that the root system consists of roots, generally below ground.

rubric.why: Anchorage holds the plant in place.
rubric.how: Explain that roots anchor the plant in soil.

rubric.why: Uptake of water and minerals is a main root function.
rubric.how: State that roots absorb water and minerals from soil.

rubric.why: Food storage is another root function where applicable.
rubric.how: Include food storage or explain how absorption supports plant growth.

modelAnswer: The root system consists of the roots of a plant and usually grows below the ground.
Roots anchor the plant in the soil.
They absorb water and minerals from the soil for the plant.
Some roots can also store food.

written.text: Q5.9. Define homeostasis and explain its importance. Discuss how different organ systems work together to maintain homeostasis.
written.finalAnswer: Homeostasis is the maintenance of stable internal conditions. It is important for normal cell and organ function. Organ systems, including the respiratory, circulatory, digestive, and excretory systems, work together to supply useful materials, transport them, and remove wastes so internal conditions remain stable.

rubric.why: A correct definition is the foundation of the response.
rubric.how: Define it as maintaining stable internal conditions.

rubric.why: The importance must connect stability with normal functioning.
rubric.how: State that cells and organs need stable conditions to work properly.

rubric.why: The question specifically asks about cooperation among systems.
rubric.how: State that several organ systems cooperate.

rubric.why: Examples show how systems supply and transport needed materials.
rubric.how: Describe a role of the respiratory, digestive, or circulatory system.

rubric.why: Waste removal and stable conditions complete the homeostasis account.
rubric.description: Explain the outcome of system cooperation.
rubric.how: Mention waste removal and maintaining stable conditions.

modelAnswer: Homeostasis is the maintenance of stable internal conditions in an organism.
It is important because cells and organs need suitable conditions to function properly.
Different organ systems work together to maintain homeostasis.
The digestive system supplies nutrients, the respiratory system supplies oxygen, and the circulatory system transports materials around the body.
The excretory system removes wastes, helping keep the internal conditions stable.

written.text: Q5.10. Describe how the respiratory and circulatory systems work together to maintain homeostasis of oxygen and carbon dioxide levels in the body.
written.finalAnswer: The respiratory system takes oxygen into the lungs and removes carbon dioxide. Oxygen passes into the blood and the circulatory system carries it to body cells. Carbon dioxide passes from cells into the blood, which carries it to the lungs for removal. This cooperation maintains suitable oxygen and carbon dioxide levels.

rubric.why: The response must explain oxygen uptake by the respiratory system.
rubric.how: State that the lungs take in oxygen.

rubric.why: Circulation delivers oxygen to tissues and cells.
rubric.how: Explain that blood carries oxygen to body cells.

rubric.why: The return path of carbon dioxide must be explained.
rubric.description: Describe carbon dioxide transport to the lungs.
rubric.how: State that blood carries carbon dioxide from cells to the lungs.

rubric.why: Removal of carbon dioxide maintains suitable gas levels.
rubric.how: State that carbon dioxide is removed and gas levels are kept stable.

modelAnswer: The respiratory system brings oxygen into the lungs, where it passes into the blood.
The circulatory system carries oxygen in the blood to body cells.
Carbon dioxide from the cells passes into the blood and is carried to the lungs.
The respiratory system removes the carbon dioxide, helping maintain suitable oxygen and carbon dioxide levels in the body.

written.text: Q5.1. How does the structure of epithelial tissue relate to its function in different parts of the body?
written.finalAnswer: Epithelial tissue forms sheets of closely arranged cells that cover surfaces and line organs. Its structure suits functions such as protection, absorption, and secretion; for example, stomach epithelium secretes mucus and digestive substances.

rubric.why: The basic arrangement and location of epithelial tissue must be described.
rubric.how: State that it forms sheets covering or lining surfaces.

rubric.why: Protection is a key function related to its covering arrangement.
rubric.description: Explain a function related to structure.
rubric.how: Connect the epithelial covering to protection.

rubric.why: Epithelia are specialised for more than one role in different sites.
rubric.how: Mention absorption or secretion.

rubric.why: A relevant body example demonstrates how function varies by location.
rubric.description: Give an example from the stomach or another body part.
rubric.how: Explain that stomach epithelium secretes mucus or digestive substances.

modelAnswer: Epithelial tissue is made of closely arranged cells that form sheets covering body surfaces and lining organs.
This arrangement provides a protective covering.
Depending on its location, epithelial tissue can also absorb substances or secrete them.
For example, stomach epithelial tissue secretes mucus, pepsinogen, and hydrochloric acid.

written.text: Q5.2. Evaluate the importance of organ systems working in harmony and predict the consequences of a failure in one system on the others.
written.finalAnswer: Organ systems must work in harmony because they depend on one another to supply materials, transport them, remove wastes, and maintain homeostasis. If one system fails, other systems may not receive what they need or may be affected by waste build-up, disrupting the whole body.

rubric.why: The answer must state the need for coordination.
rubric.how: State that organ systems work together and depend on one another.

rubric.why: Maintaining stable internal conditions is a central benefit.
rubric.how: Mention maintaining homeostasis.

rubric.why: The systems cooperate in supplying and moving useful substances.
rubric.how: Mention supplying oxygen or nutrients and transporting them.

rubric.why: The question asks for a prediction about the effect of failure.
rubric.how: Explain that failure in one system affects the functioning of others.

rubric.why: The answer must give a consequence for the organism as a whole.
rubric.how: Describe disrupted body function, waste accumulation, or loss of stable conditions.

modelAnswer: Organ systems work in harmony because each depends on the others to carry out the body's life functions.
Together, they supply and transport useful materials, remove wastes, and maintain homeostasis.
If one system fails, other systems may not receive the oxygen, nutrients, or materials they need.
Wastes may also build up if the system responsible for their removal is not working.
As a result, the function of other systems and the whole body may be disrupted.

examTips: Section A tests definitions, functions, and identification of the correct tissue or organ system; read every option carefully, especially questions about transport and secretion.
Short-answer questions usually earn marks for a precise definition, a named structure, and its function. Use key terms such as xylem, phloem, mesophyll, and homeostasis.
Long questions are commonly marked point by point. Organise answers by tissue or organ system, then state the contribution of each.
For a leaf or stomach question, name each tissue and immediately connect it to its function.
In comparison questions, write a clear difference for both items rather than describing only one.
In questions about homeostasis, explain how systems cooperate and connect their actions to stable internal conditions.

hints: Recall the two main kinds of mesophyll.
State the main role of palisade cells and the special feature of spongy cells.
yourTurn.question: Q5.4. What is the function of the palisade mesophyll in the leaf?
solution: It carries out photosynthesis in the leaf.

hints: Think of what roots take from the soil.
Name both materials that are absorbed.
yourTurn.question: Q5.8. Differentiate between the following: ii. Root system and shoot system
solution: The root system anchors the plant and absorbs water and minerals from the soil.
The shoot system includes stems, leaves, flowers, and fruits and carries out functions such as support, photosynthesis, transport, and reproduction.
yourTurn.answer: The root system anchors the plant and absorbs water and minerals; the shoot system consists of above-ground stems, leaves, flowers, and fruits and performs support, photosynthesis, transport, and reproduction.

steps.why: Begin by defining the internal balance that the question asks about.
steps.text: Homeostasis is the maintenance of stable internal conditions in an organism.

steps.why: A full answer should say why this stable condition matters.
steps.text: It is important because cells and organs need suitable conditions to function properly.

steps.why: Mentioning several systems shows that homeostasis is a coordinated process.
steps.text: Different organ systems work together to maintain homeostasis.

steps.why: The digestive, respiratory, and circulatory systems provide and distribute materials needed by cells.
steps.text: The digestive system supplies nutrients, the respiratory system supplies oxygen, and the circulatory system transports materials around the body.

steps.why: Waste removal is another important part of keeping the internal environment stable.
steps.text: The excretory system removes wastes, helping keep the internal conditions stable.

example.question: Q5.9. Define homeostasis and explain its importance. Discuss how different organ systems work together to maintain homeostasis.
example.answer: Homeostasis is the maintenance of stable internal conditions in an organism. It is important because cells and organs need suitable conditions to function properly. Different organ systems work together: the digestive system supplies nutrients, the respiratory system supplies oxygen, the circulatory system transports materials, and the excretory system removes wastes. Their coordinated actions help maintain stable internal conditions.

explain.title: Organisation from small to large
explain.body: The order is cell → tissue → organ → organ system. Cells with similar functions form tissues; different tissues work together in organs; organs cooperate in organ systems.

explain.title: Tissues perform specialised jobs
explain.body: Animal tissues include epithelial, connective, muscle, and nervous tissues. Plant tissues include epidermal tissue, mesophyll, xylem, and phloem. Their structures suit their functions.

explain.title: The stomach digests food
explain.body: Stomach epithelial tissue produces mucus, pepsinogen, and hydrochloric acid. Connective tissue supports the stomach and contains blood vessels and nerves. Smooth muscle churns food and mixes it with digestive juices.

explain.title: The leaf captures and transports materials
explain.body: Palisade mesophyll carries out most photosynthesis; spongy mesophyll has air spaces for gas exchange. Xylem brings water to the leaf, phloem carries food, and the epidermis protects the leaf.

explain.title: Organs and systems cooperate
explain.body: Plant roots anchor and absorb water and minerals, while shoot organs support photosynthesis, transport, and reproduction. In humans, organ systems cooperate to provide needed materials and remove wastes.

explain.title: Homeostasis keeps conditions stable
explain.body: Homeostasis means maintaining stable internal conditions. Systems such as the respiratory, circulatory, digestive, and excretory systems work together so cells and organs can function properly.

mistakes: Reversing the order of tissue and organ in the organisation hierarchy.
Saying xylem transports food or phloem transports water; xylem transports water and minerals, while phloem transports food.
Confusing palisade and spongy mesophyll: palisade mainly carries out photosynthesis, while spongy mesophyll has air spaces for gas exchange.
Listing stomach tissues without explaining what each does.
Defining homeostasis without explaining why it matters or how organ systems help maintain it.
Describing only one side of a comparison question instead of giving a difference between both terms.
